8 9 # mimalloc 10 11   12 13 mimalloc (pronounced "me-malloc") 14 is a general purpose allocator with excellent [performance](#performance) characteristics. 15 Initially developed by Daan Leijen for the runtime systems of the 16 [Koka](https://koka-lang.github.io) and [Lean](https://github.com/leanprover/lean) languages. 17 18 Latest release : `v3.5.0` (2026-08-18) recommended. 19 Latest v2 release: `v2.5.0` (2026-08-18) stable. 20 Latest v1 release: `v1.15.0` (2026-08-18) legacy. 21 22 mimalloc is a drop-in replacement for `malloc` and can be used in other programs 23 without code changes, for example, on dynamically linked ELF-based systems (Linux, BSD, etc.) you can use it as: 24 ``` 25 > LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/libmimalloc.so myprogram 26 ``` 27 It also includes a way to dynamically override the default allocator in [Windows](#override_on_windows). 28 Notable aspects of the design include: 29 30 - __small and consistent__: the library is about 10k LOC using simple and 31 consistent data structures. This makes it very suitable 32 to integrate and adapt in other projects. For runtime systems it 33 provides hooks for a monotonic _heartbeat_ and deferred freeing (for 34 bounded worst-case times with reference counting). 35 Partly due to its simplicity, mimalloc has been ported to many systems (Windows, macOS, 36 Linux, WASM, various BSD's, Haiku, MUSL, etc) and has excellent support for dynamic overriding. 37 At the same time, it is an industrial strength allocator that runs (very) large scale 38 distributed services on thousands of machines with excellent worst case latencies. 39 - __free list sharding__: instead of one big free list (per size class) we have 40 many smaller lists per "mimalloc page" which reduces fragmentation and 41 increases locality -- 42 things that are allocated close in time get allocated close in memory. 43 (A mimalloc page contains blocks of one size class and is usually 64KiB on a 64-bit system). 44 - __free list multi-sharding__: the big idea! Not only do we shard the free list 45 per mimalloc page, but for each page we have multiple free lists. In particular, there 46 is one list for thread-local `free` operations, and another one for concurrent `free` 47 operations. Free-ing from another thread can now be a single CAS without needing 48 sophisticated coordination between threads. Since there will be 49 thousands of separate free lists, contention is naturally distributed over the heap, 50 and the chance of contending on a single location will be low -- this is quite 51 similar to randomized algorithms like skip lists where adding 52 a random oracle removes the need for a more complex algorithm. 53 - __eager page purging__: when a "page" becomes empty (with increased chance 54 due to free list sharding) the memory is marked to the OS as unused (reset or decommitted) 55 reducing (real) memory pressure and fragmentation, especially in long running 56 programs. 57 - __secure__: _mimalloc_ can be built in secure mode, adding guard pages, 58 randomized allocation, encrypted free lists, etc. to protect against various 59 heap vulnerabilities. The performance penalty is usually around 10% on average 60 over our benchmarks. 61 - __first-class heaps__: efficiently create and use multiple heaps to allocate across different regions. 62 A heap can be destroyed at once instead of deallocating each object separately. 63 New: v3 has true first-class heaps where one can allocate in a heap from any thread. 64 - __bounded__: it does not suffer from _blowup_ \[1\], has bounded worst-case allocation 65 times (_wcat_) (upto OS primitives), bounded space overhead (~0.2% meta-data, with low 66 internal fragmentation), and has no internal points of contention using only atomic operations. 67 - __fast__: In our benchmarks (see [below](#performance)), 68 _mimalloc_ outperforms other leading allocators (_jemalloc_, _tcmalloc_, _Hoard_, etc), 69 and often uses less memory. A nice property is that it does consistently well over a wide range 70 of benchmarks. There is also good huge OS page support for larger server programs. 71 72 The [documentation](https://microsoft.github.io/mimalloc) gives a full overview of the API. 73 You can read more on the design of mimalloc in the [technical report](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/mimalloc-free-list-sharding-in-action) which also has detailed benchmark results. 74 75 Enjoy! 76 77 ### Versions 78 79 There are three maintained versions of mimalloc. Set this to 2 (default) to 360 only enable this on overcommit systems (e.g. Linux). Set this to 1 to enable explicitly on other systems 361 as well (like Windows or macOS) which may improve performance (as the whole arena is committed at once). 362 Note that eager commit only increases the commit but not the actual the peak resident set 363 (rss) so it is generally ok to enable this. 364 - `MIMALLOC_PURGE_DELAY=N`: the delay in `N` milli-seconds (by default `1000` in v3) after which mimalloc will purge 365 OS pages that are not in use. This signals to the OS that the underlying physical memory can be reused which 366 can reduce memory fragmentation especially in long running (server) programs. Setting `N` to `0` purges immediately when 367 a page becomes unused which can improve memory usage but also decreases performance. 368 Setting it to `-1` disables purging completely. 369 - `MIMALLOC_PURGE_DECOMMITS=1`: By default "purging" memory means unused memory is decommitted (`MEM_DECOMMIT` on Windows, 370 `MADV_DONTNEED` (which decresease rss immediately) on `mmap` systems). Set this to 0 to instead "reset" unused 371 memory on a purge (`MEM_RESET` on Windows, generally `MADV_FREE` (which does not decrease rss immediately) on `mmap` systems). 372 Mimalloc generally does not "free" OS memory but only "purges" OS memory, in other words, it tries to keep virtual 373 address ranges and decommits within those ranges (to make the underlying physical memory available to other processes). 374 375 Further options for large workloads and services: 376 377 - `MIMALLOC_ALLOW_THP=1`: By default always allow transparent huge pages (THP) on Linux systems. This build enables various mitigations 412 to make mimalloc more robust against exploits. In particular: 413 414 - All internal mimalloc page meta-data is surrounded by guard pages (so a buffer overflow exploit cannot reach into the metadata). 415 - All free list pointers are 416 [encoded](https://github.com/microsoft/mimalloc/blob/783e3377f79ee82af43a0793910a9f2d01ac7863/include/mimalloc-internal.h#L396) 417 with per-page keys which is used both to prevent overwrites with a known pointer, as well as to detect heap corruption. 418 - Double free's are detected (and ignored). 419 - The free lists are initialized in a random order and allocation randomly chooses between extension and reuse within a page to 420 mitigate against attacks that rely on a predicable allocation order. Similarly, the larger heap blocks allocated by mimalloc 421 from the OS are also address randomized. 422 - If enabling `-DMI_SECURE_FULL=ON` there will also be guard pages at the end of each (64KiB) mimalloc page (thus interleaving 423 valid block data with inaccessible gaps). This setting is not recommended in general as it is more expensive and can lead to 424 reaching the maximum VMA limit on Linux systems if the heap gets too large. 425 426 As always, evaluate with care as part of an overall security strategy as all of the above are mitigations but not guarantees. 427 428 ## Debug Mode 429 430 When _mimalloc_ is built using debug mode, (`-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug`), 431 various checks are done at runtime to catch development errors. 432 433 - Statistics are maintained in detail for each object size. They can be shown using `MIMALLOC_SHOW_STATS=1` at runtime. 434 - All objects have padding at the end to detect (byte precise) heap block overflows. 435 - Double free's, and freeing invalid heap pointers are detected. 436 - Corrupted free-lists and some forms of use-after-free are detected. 437 438 ## Guarded Mode 439 440 _mimalloc_ can be build in guarded mode using the `-DMI_GUARDED=ON` flags in `cmake`. 441 This is `ON` by default when building a debug version of mimalloc. 442 Guarded mode enables placing OS guard pages behind certain object allocations to catch buffer overflows as they occur. 443 This can be invaluable to catch buffer-overflow bugs in large programs. However, it also means that any object 444 allocated with a guard page takes at least 8 KiB memory for the guard page and its alignment. As such, allocating 445 a guard page for every allocation may be too expensive both in terms of memory, and in terms of performance with 446 many system calls. Therefore, there are various environment variables (and options) to tune this: 447 448 - `MIMALLOC_GUARDED_SAMPLE_RATE=N`: Set the sample rate to `N` (by default 0). This mode places a guard page 449 behind every `N` suitable object allocations (per thread). Since the performance in guarded mode without placing 450 guard pages is close to release mode, this can be used to enable guard pages even in production to catch latent 451 buffer overflow bugs. Set the sample rate to `1` to guard every object, and to `0` to place no guard pages at all. 452 453 - `MIMALLOC_GUARDED_SAMPLE_SEED=N`: Start sampling at `N` (by default random). Can be used to reproduce a buffer 454 overflow if needed. 455 456 - `MIMALLOC_GUARDED_MIN=N`, `MIMALLOC_GUARDED_MAX=N`: Minimal and maximal _rounded_ object sizes for which a guard 457 page is considered (`0` and `1GiB` respectively). If you suspect a buffer overflow occurs with an object of size 458 141, set the minimum and maximum to `148` and the sample rate to `1` to have all of those guarded. 459 460 - `MIMALLOC_GUARDED_PRECISE=1`: If we have an object of size 13, we would usually place it an aligned 16 bytes in 461 front of the guard page. Using `MIMALLOC_GUARDED_PRECISE` places it exactly 13 bytes before a page so that even 462 a 1 byte overflow is detected. This violates the C/C++ minimal alignment guarantees though so use with care. 463 464 465 # Overriding Standard Malloc 466 467 Overriding the standard `malloc` (and `new`) can be done either _dynamically_ or _statically_. 468 469 ## Dynamic override 470 471 This is the recommended way to override the standard malloc interface. 472 473 ### Dynamic Override on Linux, BSD 474 475 On these ELF-based systems we preload the mimalloc shared 476 library so all calls to the standard `malloc` interface are 477 resolved to the _mimalloc_ library. 478 ``` 479 > env LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/libmimalloc.so myprogram 480 ``` 481 482 You can set extra environment variables to check that mimalloc is running, 483 like: 484 ``` 485 > env MIMALLOC_VERBOSE=1 LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/libmimalloc.so myprogram 486 ``` 487 or run with the debug version to get detailed statistics: 488 ``` 489 > env MIMALLOC_SHOW_STATS=1 LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/libmimalloc-debug.so myprogram 490 ``` 491 492 ### Dynamic Override on MacOS 493 494 On macOS we can also preload the mimalloc shared 495 library so all calls to the standard `malloc` interface are 496 resolved to the _mimalloc_ library. 497 ``` 498 > env DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES=/usr/lib/libmimalloc.dylib myprogram 499 ``` 500 501 Note that certain security restrictions may apply when doing this from 502 the [shell](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/43941322/dyld-insert-libraries-ignored-when-calling-application-through-bash). 503 504 505 ### Dynamic Override on Windows 506 507 We use a separate redirection DLL to override mimalloc on Windows 508 such that we redirect all malloc/free calls that go through the (dynamic) C runtime allocator, 509 including those from other DLL's or libraries. As it intercepts all allocation calls on a low level, 510 it can be used on large programs that include other 3rd party components. 511 There are four requirements to make the overriding work well: 512 513 1. Use the C-runtime library as a DLL (using the `/MD` or `/MDd` switch). 514 515 2. Link your program explicitly with the `mimalloc.dll.lib` export library for the `mimalloc.dll`. 516 (which must be compiled with `-DMI_OVERRIDE=ON`, which is the default though). 517 To ensure the `mimalloc.dll` is actually loaded at run-time it is easiest 518 to insert some call to the mimalloc API in the `main` function, like `mi_version()` 519 (or use the `/include:mi_version` switch on the linker command, or 520 similarly, `#pragma comment(linker, "/include:mi_version")` in some source file). 521 See the `mimalloc-test-override` project for an example on how to use this. 522 523 3. The `mimalloc-redirect.dll` must be put in the same directory as the main 524 `mimalloc.dll` at runtime (as it is a dependency of that DLL). 525 The redirection DLL ensures that all calls to the C runtime malloc API get 526 redirected to mimalloc functions (which reside in `mimalloc.dll`). 527 528 4. Ensure the `mimalloc.dll` comes as early as possible in the import 529 list of the final executable (so it can intercept all potential allocations). 530 You can use `minject -l ` to check this if needed. 531 532 For best performance on Windows with C++, it is also recommended to also override 533 the `new`/`delete` operations (by including [`mimalloc-new-delete.h`](include/mimalloc-new-delete.h) 534 a single(!) source file in your project). 535 536 The environment variable `MIMALLOC_DISABLE_REDIRECT=1` can be used to disable dynamic 537 overriding at run-time. Use `MIMALLOC_VERBOSE=1` to check if mimalloc was successfully 538 redirected. 539 540 For different platforms than x64, you may need a specific [redirection dll](bin). 541 Furthermore, we cannot always re-link an executable or ensure `mimalloc.dll` comes 542 first in the import table. In such cases the [`minject`](bin) tool can be used 543 to patch the executable's import tables. 544 545 546 ## Static override 547 548 On Unix-like systems, you can also statically link with _mimalloc_ to override the standard 549 malloc interface. The recommended way is to link the final program with the 550 _mimalloc_ single object file (`mimalloc.o`). We use 551 an object file instead of a library file as linkers give preference to 552 that over archives to resolve symbols. To ensure that the standard 553 malloc interface resolves to the _mimalloc_ library, link it as the first 554 object file. For example: 555 556 ``` 557 > gcc -o myprogram mimalloc.o myfile1.c ... 558 ``` 559 560 Another way to override statically that works on all platforms, is to 561 link statically to mimalloc (as shown in the introduction) and include a 562 header file in each source file that re-defines `malloc` etc. to `mi_malloc`. 563 This is provided by [`mimalloc-override.h`](include/mimalloc-override.h). This only works 564 reliably though if all sources are 565 under your control or otherwise mixing of pointers from different heaps may occur! 566 567 Note: recently we also enabled static overloading on Windows. In that case you need 568 to link with the static CRT _release_ runtime (`/MT`) and link with the static 569 `mimalloc(-debug).obj` (to take precendence over the definitions in the CRT library). 570 571 # Tools 572 573 Generally, we recommend using the standard allocator with memory tracking tools, but mimalloc 574 can also be build to support the [address sanitizer][asan] or the excellent [Valgrind] tool. 575 Moreover, it can be build to support Windows event tracing ([ETW]). 576 This has a small performance overhead but does allow detecting memory leaks and byte-precise 577 buffer overflows directly on final executables. See also the `test/test-wrong.c` file to test with various tools. 578 579 ## Valgrind 580 581 To build with [valgrind] support, use the `MI_TRACK_VALGRIND=ON` cmake option: 582 583 ``` 584 > cmake ../.. -DMI_TRACK_VALGRIND=ON 585 ``` 586 587 This can also be combined with secure mode or debug mode. 588 You can then run your programs directly under valgrind: 589 590 ``` 591 > valgrind 592 ``` 593 594 If you rely on overriding `malloc`/`free` by mimalloc (instead of using the `mi_malloc`/`mi_free` API directly), 595 you also need to tell `valgrind` to not intercept those calls itself, and use: 596 597 ``` 598 > MIMALLOC_SHOW_STATS=1 valgrind --soname-synonyms=somalloc=*mimalloc* -- 599 ``` 600 601 By setting the `MIMALLOC_SHOW_STATS` environment variable you can check that mimalloc is indeed 602 used and not the standard allocator. Even though the [Valgrind option][valgrind-soname] 603 is called `--soname-synonyms`, this also works when overriding with a static library or object file. 604 To dynamically override mimalloc using `LD_PRELOAD` together with `valgrind`, use: 605 606 ``` 607 > valgrind --trace-children=yes --soname-synonyms=somalloc=*mimalloc* /usr/bin/env LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/libmimalloc.so -- 608 ``` 609 610 See also the `test/test-wrong.c` file to test with `valgrind`. 611 612 Valgrind support is in its initial development -- please report any issues. 613 614 [Valgrind]: https://valgrind.org/ 615 [valgrind-soname]: https://valgrind.org/docs/manual/manual-core.html#opt.soname-synonyms 616 617 ## ASAN 618 619 To build with the address sanitizer, use the `-DMI_TRACK_ASAN=ON` cmake option: 620 621 ``` 622 > cmake ../.. -DMI_TRACK_ASAN=ON 623 ``` 624 625 This can also be combined with secure mode or debug mode. 626 You can then run your programs as:' 627 628 ``` 629 > ASAN_OPTIONS=verbosity=1 630 ``` 631 632 When you link a program with an address sanitizer build of mimalloc, you should 633 generally compile that program too with the address sanitizer enabled. 634 For example, assuming you build mimalloc in `out/debug`: 635 636 ``` 637 clang -g -o test-wrong -Iinclude test/test-wrong.c out/debug/libmimalloc-asan-debug.a -lpthread -fsanitize=address -fsanitize-recover=address 638 ``` 639 640 Since the address sanitizer redirects the standard allocation functions, on some platforms (macOSX for example) 641 it is required to compile mimalloc with `-DMI_OVERRIDE=OFF`. 642 Address sanitizer support is in its initial development -- please report any issues. 643 644 [asan]: https://github.com/google/sanitizers/wiki/AddressSanitizer 645 646 ## ETW 647 648 Event tracing for Windows ([ETW]) provides a high performance way to capture all allocations though 649 mimalloc and analyze them later. To build with ETW support, use the `-DMI_TRACK_ETW=ON` cmake option. 650 651 You can then capture an allocation trace using the Windows performance recorder (WPR), using the 652 `src/prim/windows/etw-mimalloc.wprp` profile. In our benchmark suite, _mimalloc_ outperforms other leading 673 allocators (_jemalloc_, _tcmalloc_, _Hoard_, etc), and has a similar memory footprint. A nice property is that it 674 does consistently well over the wide range of benchmarks. 675 676 General memory allocators are interesting as there exists no algorithm that is 677 optimal -- for a given allocator one can usually construct a workload 678 where it does not do so well. The goal is thus to find an allocation 679 strategy that performs well over a wide range of benchmarks without 680 suffering from (too much) underperformance in less common situations. 681 682 As always, interpret these results with care since some benchmarks test synthetic 683 or uncommon situations that may never apply to your workloads. For example, most 684 allocators do not do well on `xmalloc-testN` but that includes even the best 685 industrial allocators like _jemalloc_ and _tcmalloc_ that are used in some of 686 the world's largest systems (like Chrome or FreeBSD). 687 688 Also, the benchmarks here do not measure the behaviour on very large and long-running server workloads, 689 or worst-case latencies of allocation. Much work has gone into `mimalloc` to work well on such 690 workloads (for example, to reduce virtual memory fragmentation on long-running services) 691 but such optimizations are not always reflected in the current benchmark suite. 692 693 We show here only an overview -- for 694 more specific details and further benchmarks we refer to the 695 [technical report](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/mimalloc-free-list-sharding-in-action). 696 The benchmark suite is automated and available separately 697 as # mimalloc   mimalloc (pronounced "me-malloc") is a general purpose allocator with excellent [performance](#performance) characteristics. Initially developed by Daan Leijen for the runtime systems of the [Koka](https://koka-lang.github.io) and [Lean](https://github.com/leanprover/lean) languages. Latest release : `v3.5.0` (2026-08-18) recommended. Latest v2 release: `v2.5.0` (2026-08-18) stable. Latest v1 release: `v1.15.0` (2026-08-18) legacy. mimalloc is a drop-in replacement for `malloc` and can be used in other programs without code changes, for example, on dynamically linked ELF-based systems (Linux, BSD, etc.) you can use it as: ``` > LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/libmimalloc.so myprogram ``` It also includes a way to dynamically override the default allocator in [Windows](#override_on_windows). Notable aspects of the design include: - __small and consistent__: the library is about 10k LOC using simple and consistent data structures. This makes it very suitable to integrate and adapt in other projects. For runtime systems it provides hooks for a monotonic _heartbeat_ and deferred freeing (for bounded worst-case times with reference counting). Partly due to its simplicity, mimalloc has been ported to many systems (Windows, macOS, Linux, WASM, various BSD's, Haiku, MUSL, etc) and has excellent support for dynamic overriding. At the same time, it is an industrial strength allocator that runs (very) large scale distributed services on thousands of machines with excellent worst case latencies. - __free list sharding__: instead of one big free list (per size class) we have many smaller lists per "mimalloc page" which reduces fragmentation and increases locality -- things that are allocated close in time get allocated close in memory. (A mimalloc page contains blocks of one size class and is usually 64KiB on a 64-bit system). - __free list multi-sharding__: the big idea! Not only do we shard the free list per mimalloc page, but for each page we have multiple free lists. In particular, there is one list for thread-local `free` operations, and another one for concurrent `free` operations. Free-ing from another thread can now be a single CAS without needing sophisticated coordination between threads. Since there will be thousands of separate free lists, contention is naturally distributed over the heap, and the chance of contending on a single location will be low -- this is quite similar to randomized algorithms like skip lists where adding a random oracle removes the need for a more complex algorithm. - __eager page purging__: when a "page" becomes empty (with increased chance due to free list sharding) the memory is marked to the OS as unused (reset or decommitted) reducing (real) memory pressure and fragmentation, especially in long running programs. - __secure__: _mimalloc_ can be built in secure mode, adding guard pages, randomized allocation, encrypted free lists, etc. to protect against various heap vulnerabilities. The performance penalty is usually around 10% on average over our benchmarks. - __first-class heaps__: efficiently create and use multiple heaps to allocate across different regions. A heap can be destroyed at once instead of deallocating each object separately. New: v3 has true first-class heaps where one can allocate in a heap from any thread. - __bounded__: it does not suffer from _blowup_ \[1\], has bounded worst-case allocation times (_wcat_) (upto OS primitives), bounded space overhead (~0.2% meta-data, with low internal fragmentation), and has no internal points of contention using only atomic operations. - __fast__: In our benchmarks (see [below](#performance)), _mimalloc_ outperforms other leading allocators (_jemalloc_, _tcmalloc_, _Hoard_, etc), and often uses less memory. A nice property is that it does consistently well over a wide range of benchmarks. There is also good huge OS page support for larger server programs. The [documentation](https://microsoft.github.io/mimalloc) gives a full overview of the API. You can read more on the design of mimalloc in the [technical report](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/mimalloc-free-list-sharding-in-action) which also has detailed benchmark results. Enjoy! ### Versions There are three maintained versions of mimalloc. These are mostly equal except for how the OS memory is handled. New development is mostly on v3, while v1 and v2 are maintained with security and bug fixes. - __v3__: recommended: simplifies the lock-free design of previous versions and improves sharing of memory between threads. On certain large workloads this version may use (much) less memory. Also supports true first-class heaps (that can allocate from any thread) and has more efficient heap-walking (for the CPython GC for example). (release tags: `v3.x`, development branch `dev3`). - __v2__: stable mimalloc version. Uses thread-local segments to reduce fragmentation. (release tags: `v2.x`, development branch `dev2` and `main`) - __v1__: legacy version: initial design of mimalloc (release tags: `v1.x`, development branch `dev`). __Send PR's against this version if possible.__ ### Releases * 2026-08-18, `v1.15.0`, `v2.5.0`, `v3.5.0`: (v3) slightly better performance for `free` using aligned chunks, cleanup cmake options, require armv8.3 (with MI_OPT_ARCH) for faster load-acquire, increase retired page count from 1 to 3, faster double free detection in secure mode, use faster atomics for the arena bitmaps (thank you Alan Andrade, #1346), faster pagemap lookup. Various bugs found by DeepTest include: fix offset for `mi_heap_realloc_aligned`, fix `mi_(w)dupenv_s` buffer size, fix potential overflow in size options, and error codes for `mi_reallocarr(ay)`. * 2026-02-03, `v3.2.8` (rc3): Fix thread reinitialize issue on macOS. Fix SIMD codegen bug on older GCC versions. Extend Windows TLS slot limit from 64 to 1088. Report commit statistics more precise. Fixes issue in free-page search in arenas. * 2026-01-15, `v1.9.7`, `v2.2.7`, `v3.2.7` (rc2): Fix zero initializing blocks that were OS allocated. For v3 various bug and performance fixes. Fix Debian 32-bit compilation. * 2026-01-08, `v1.9.6`, `v2.2.6`, `v3.2.6` (rc1): Important bug fixes. Many improvements to v3 including true first-class heaps where one can allocate in heap from any thread, and track statistics per heap as well. Added `MIMALLOC_ALLOW_THP` option. This is by default enabled except on Android. When THP is detected on v3, mimalloc will set the `MIMALLOC_MINIMAL_PURGE_SIZE` to 2MiB to avoid breaking up potential THP huge pages. v3 uses faster TLS access on Windows, and has improved performance for `mi_calloc` and aligned allocations. Fixed rare race condition on older v3, fixed potential buffer overflow in debug statistics, add API for returning allocated sizes on allocation and free. * [Older release notes](#older-release-notes) Special thanks to: * Sergiy Kuryata for his contributions on reducing memory commit -- especially on Windows with the Windows thread pool (now implemented in v3). * [David Carlier](https://devnexen.blogspot.com/) (@devnexen) for his many contributions, and making mimalloc work better on many less common operating systems, like Haiku, Dragonfly, etc. * Mary Feofanova (@mary3000), Evgeniy Moiseenko, and Manuel Pöter (@mpoeter) for making mimalloc TSAN checkable, and finding memory model bugs using the [genMC] model checker. * Weipeng Liu (@pongba), Zhuowei Li, Junhua Wang, and Jakub Szymanski, for their early support of mimalloc and deployment at large scale services, leading to many improvements in the mimalloc algorithms for large workloads. * Jason Gibson (@jasongibson) for exhaustive testing on large scale workloads and server environments, and finding complex bugs in (early versions of) `mimalloc`. * Manuel Pöter (@mpoeter) and Sam Gross(@colesbury) for finding an ABA concurrency issue in abandoned segment reclamation. Sam also created the [no GIL](https://github.com/colesbury/nogil) Python fork which uses mimalloc internally. [genMC]: https://plv.mpi-sws.org/genmc/ ### Usage mimalloc is used in various large scale low-latency services and programs, for example: # Building ## Windows Open `ide/vs2022/mimalloc.sln` in Visual Studio 2022 and build. The `mimalloc-lib` project builds a static library (in `out/msvc-x64`), while the `mimalloc-override-dll` project builds a DLL for overriding malloc in the entire program. ## Linux, macOS, BSD, etc. We use [`cmake`](https://cmake.org) as the build system: ``` > mkdir -p out/release > cd out/release > cmake ../.. > make ``` This builds the library as a shared (dynamic) library (`.so` or `.dylib`), a static library (`.a`), and as a single object file (`.o`). `> sudo make install` (install the library and header files in `/usr/local/lib` and `/usr/local/include`) You can build the debug version which does many internal checks and maintains detailed statistics as: ``` > mkdir -p out/debug > cd out/debug > cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug ../.. > make ``` This will name the shared library as `libmimalloc-debug.so`. Finally, you can build a _secure_ version that uses guard pages, encrypted free lists, etc., as: ``` > mkdir -p out/secure > cd out/secure > cmake -DMI_SECURE=ON ../.. > make ``` This will name the shared library as `libmimalloc-secure.so`. Use `cmake ../.. -LH` to see all the available build options. The examples use the default compiler. If you like to use another, use: ``` > CC=clang CXX=clang++ cmake ../.. ``` ## Cmake with Visual Studio You can also use cmake on Windows. Open a Visual Studio 2022 development prompt and invoke `cmake` with the right [generator](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/generator/Visual%20Studio%2017%202022.html) and architecture, like: ``` > cmake ..\.. -G "Visual Studio 17 2022" -A x64 -DMI_OVERRIDE=ON ``` The cmake build type is specified when actually building, for example: ``` > cmake --build . --config=Release ``` You can also install the [LLVM toolset](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/build/clang-support-msbuild?view=msvc-170#install-1) on Windows to build with the `clang-cl` compiler directly: ``` > cmake ../.. -G "Visual Studio 17 2022" -T ClangCl ``` ## Single Source You can also directly build the single `src/static.c` file as part of your project without needing `cmake` at all. Make sure to also add the mimalloc `include` directory to the include path. # Using the Library The preferred usage is including ``, linking with the shared- or static library, and using the `mi_malloc` API exclusively for allocation. For example, ``` > gcc -o myprogram -lmimalloc myfile.c ``` mimalloc uses only safe OS calls (`mmap` and `VirtualAlloc`) and can co-exist with other allocators linked to the same program. If you use `cmake`, you can simply use: ``` find_package(mimalloc 1.8 REQUIRED) ``` in your `CMakeLists.txt` to find a locally installed mimalloc. Then use either: ``` target_link_libraries(myapp PUBLIC mimalloc) ``` to link with the shared (dynamic) library, or: ``` target_link_libraries(myapp PUBLIC mimalloc-static) ``` to link with the static library. See `test\CMakeLists.txt` for an example. For best performance in C++ programs, it is also recommended to override the global `new` and `delete` operators. For convenience, mimalloc provides [`mimalloc-new-delete.h`](include/mimalloc-new-delete.h) which does this for you -- just include it in a single(!) source file in your project. In C++, mimalloc also provides the `mi_stl_allocator` struct which implements the `std::allocator` interface. You can pass environment variables to print verbose messages (`MIMALLOC_VERBOSE=1`) and statistics (`MIMALLOC_SHOW_STATS=1`) (in the debug version): ``` > env MIMALLOC_SHOW_STATS=1 ./cfrac 175451865205073170563711388363 175451865205073170563711388363 = 374456281610909315237213 * 468551 subproc 0 blocks peak total current block total# bin S 4: 75.3 KiB 55.2 MiB 0 32 B 1.8 M ok bin S 6: 31.0 KiB 180.4 KiB 0 48 B 3.8 K ok bin S 8: 64 B 64 B 0 64 B 1 ok bin S 9: 160 B 160 B 0 80 B 2 ok bin S 17: 1.2 KiB 1.2 KiB 0 320 B 4 ok bin S 21: 640 B 3.1 KiB 0 640 B 5 ok bin S 33: 5.0 KiB 5.0 KiB 0 5.0 KiB 1 ok binned : 84.2 Ki 41.5 Mi 0 ok huge : 0 0 0 ok total : 84.2 KiB 41.5 MiB 0 malloc req: 29.7 MiB pages peak total current block total# touched : 152.8 KiB 152.8 KiB 152.8 KiB pages : 8 14 0 ok abandoned : 1 249 0 ok reclaima : 0 reclaimf : 249 reabandon : 0 waits : 0 extended : 38 retire : 35 searches : 0.7 avg arenas peak total current block total# reserved : 1.0 GiB 1.0 GiB 1.0 GiB committed : 4.8 MiB 4.8 MiB 4.4 MiB reset : 0 purged : 385.5 Ki arenas : 1 rollback : 0 mmaps : 3 commits : 0 resets : 1 purges : 2 guarded : 0 heaps : 1 1 1 process peak total current block total# threads : 1 1 1 numa nodes: 1 elapsed : 0.553 s process : user: 0.557 s, system: 0.013 s, faults: 29, peak rss: 2.1 MiB, peak commit: 4.8 MiB ``` The above model of using the `mi_` prefixed API is not always possible though in existing programs that already use the standard malloc interface, and another option is to override the standard malloc interface completely and redirect all calls to the _mimalloc_ library instead . ## Environment Options You can set further options either programmatically (using [`mi_option_set`](https://microsoft.github.io/mimalloc/group__options.html)), or via environment variables: - `MIMALLOC_SHOW_STATS=1`: show statistics when the program terminates. - `MIMALLOC_VERBOSE=1`: show verbose messages (including statistics). - `MIMALLOC_SHOW_ERRORS=1`: show error and warning messages. Advanced options: - `MIMALLOC_ARENA_EAGER_COMMIT=2`: turns on eager commit for the large arenas (usually 1GiB) from which mimalloc allocates segments and pages. Set this to 2 (default) to only enable this on overcommit systems (e.g. Linux). Set this to 1 to enable explicitly on other systems as well (like Windows or macOS) which may improve performance (as the whole arena is committed at once). Note that eager commit only increases the commit but not the actual the peak resident set (rss) so it is generally ok to enable this. - `MIMALLOC_PURGE_DELAY=N`: the delay in `N` milli-seconds (by default `1000` in v3) after which mimalloc will purge OS pages that are not in use. This signals to the OS that the underlying physical memory can be reused which can reduce memory fragmentation especially in long running (server) programs. Setting `N` to `0` purges immediately when a page becomes unused which can improve memory usage but also decreases performance. Setting it to `-1` disables purging completely. - `MIMALLOC_PURGE_DECOMMITS=1`: By default "purging" memory means unused memory is decommitted (`MEM_DECOMMIT` on Windows, `MADV_DONTNEED` (which decresease rss immediately) on `mmap` systems). Set this to 0 to instead "reset" unused memory on a purge (`MEM_RESET` on Windows, generally `MADV_FREE` (which does not decrease rss immediately) on `mmap` systems). Mimalloc generally does not "free" OS memory but only "purges" OS memory, in other words, it tries to keep virtual address ranges and decommits within those ranges (to make the underlying physical memory available to other processes). Further options for large workloads and services: - `MIMALLOC_ALLOW_THP=1`: By default always allow transparent huge pages (THP) on Linux systems. On Android only this is by default off. When set to `0`, THP is disabled for the process that mimalloc runs in. If enabled, mimalloc also sets the `MIMALLOC_MINIMAL_PURGE_SIZE` in v3 to 2MiB to avoid potentially breaking up transparent huge pages when purging memory. - `MIMALLOC_USE_NUMA_NODES=N`: pretend there are at most `N` NUMA nodes. If not set, the actual NUMA nodes are detected at runtime. Setting `N` to 1 may avoid problems in some virtual environments. Also, setting it to a lower number than the actual NUMA nodes is fine and will only cause threads to potentially allocate more memory across actual NUMA nodes (but this can happen in any case as NUMA local allocation is always a best effort but not guaranteed). - `MIMALLOC_ALLOW_LARGE_OS_PAGES=0`: Set to 1 to use large OS pages (2 or 4MiB) when available; for some workloads this can significantly improve performance. However, large OS pages cannot be purged or shared with other processes so may lead to increased memory usage in some cases. Use `MIMALLOC_VERBOSE` to check if the large OS pages are enabled -- usually one needs to explicitly give permissions for large OS pages (as on [Windows][windows-huge] and [Linux][linux-huge]). However, sometimes the OS is very slow to reserve contiguous physical memory for large OS pages so use with care on systems that can have fragmented memory (for that reason, we generally recommend to use `MIMALLOC_RESERVE_HUGE_OS_PAGES` instead whenever possible). - `MIMALLOC_RESERVE_HUGE_OS_PAGES=N`: where `N` is the number of 1GiB _huge_ OS pages. This reserves the huge pages at startup and sometimes this can give a large (latency) performance improvement on big workloads. Usually it is better to not use `MIMALLOC_ALLOW_LARGE_OS_PAGES=1` in combination with this setting. Just like large OS pages, use with care as reserving contiguous physical memory can take a long time when memory is fragmented (but reserving the huge pages is done at startup only once). Note that we usually need to explicitly give permission for huge OS pages (as on [Windows][windows-huge] and [Linux][linux-huge])). The huge pages are usually allocated evenly among NUMA nodes. We can use `MIMALLOC_RESERVE_HUGE_OS_PAGES_AT=N` where `N` is the numa node (starting at 0) to allocate all the huge pages at a specific numa node instead. Use caution when using `fork` in combination with either large or huge OS pages: on a fork, the OS uses copy-on-write for all pages in the original process including the huge OS pages. When any memory is now written in that area, the OS will copy the entire 1GiB huge page (or 2MiB large page) which can cause the memory usage to grow in large increments. [linux-huge]: https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_enterprise_linux/5/html/tuning_and_optimizing_red_hat_enterprise_linux_for_oracle_9i_and_10g_databases/sect-oracle_9i_and_10g_tuning_guide-large_memory_optimization_big_pages_and_huge_pages-configuring_huge_pages_in_red_hat_enterprise_linux_4_or_5 [windows-huge]: https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/database-engine/configure-windows/enable-the-lock-pages-in-memory-option-windows?view=sql-server-2017 ## Secure Mode _mimalloc_ can be build in secure mode by using the `-DMI_SECURE=ON` flags in `cmake`. This build enables various mitigations to make mimalloc more robust against exploits. In particular: - All internal mimalloc page meta-data is surrounded by guard pages (so a buffer overflow exploit cannot reach into the metadata). - All free list pointers are [encoded](https://github.com/microsoft/mimalloc/blob/783e3377f79ee82af43a0793910a9f2d01ac7863/include/mimalloc-internal.h#L396) with per-page keys which is used both to prevent overwrites with a known pointer, as well as to detect heap corruption. - Double free's are detected (and ignored). - The free lists are initialized in a random order and allocation randomly chooses between extension and reuse within a page to mitigate against attacks that rely on a predicable allocation order. Similarly, the larger heap blocks allocated by mimalloc from the OS are also address randomized. - If enabling `-DMI_SECURE_FULL=ON` there will also be guard pages at the end of each (64KiB) mimalloc page (thus interleaving valid block data with inaccessible gaps). This setting is not recommended in general as it is more expensive and can lead to reaching the maximum VMA limit on Linux systems if the heap gets too large. As always, evaluate with care as part of an overall security strategy as all of the above are mitigations but not guarantees. ## Debug Mode When _mimalloc_ is built using debug mode, (`-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug`), various checks are done at runtime to catch development errors. - Statistics are maintained in detail for each object size. They can be shown using `MIMALLOC_SHOW_STATS=1` at runtime. - All objects have padding at the end to detect (byte precise) heap block overflows. - Double free's, and freeing invalid heap pointers are detected. - Corrupted free-lists and some forms of use-after-free are detected. ## Guarded Mode _mimalloc_ can be build in guarded mode using the `-DMI_GUARDED=ON` flags in `cmake`. This is `ON` by default when building a debug version of mimalloc. Guarded mode enables placing OS guard pages behind certain object allocations to catch buffer overflows as they occur. This can be invaluable to catch buffer-overflow bugs in large programs. However, it also means that any object allocated with a guard page takes at least 8 KiB memory for the guard page and its alignment. As such, allocating a guard page for every allocation may be too expensive both in terms of memory, and in terms of performance with many system calls. Therefore, there are various environment variables (and options) to tune this: - `MIMALLOC_GUARDED_SAMPLE_RATE=N`: Set the sample rate to `N` (by default 0). This mode places a guard page behind every `N` suitable object allocations (per thread). Since the performance in guarded mode without placing guard pages is close to release mode, this can be used to enable guard pages even in production to catch latent buffer overflow bugs. Set the sample rate to `1` to guard every object, and to `0` to place no guard pages at all. - `MIMALLOC_GUARDED_SAMPLE_SEED=N`: Start sampling at `N` (by default random). Can be used to reproduce a buffer overflow if needed. - `MIMALLOC_GUARDED_MIN=N`, `MIMALLOC_GUARDED_MAX=N`: Minimal and maximal _rounded_ object sizes for which a guard page is considered (`0` and `1GiB` respectively). If you suspect a buffer overflow occurs with an object of size 141, set the minimum and maximum to `148` and the sample rate to `1` to have all of those guarded. - `MIMALLOC_GUARDED_PRECISE=1`: If we have an object of size 13, we would usually place it an aligned 16 bytes in front of the guard page. Using `MIMALLOC_GUARDED_PRECISE` places it exactly 13 bytes before a page so that even a 1 byte overflow is detected. This violates the C/C++ minimal alignment guarantees though so use with care. # Overriding Standard Malloc Overriding the standard `malloc` (and `new`) can be done either _dynamically_ or _statically_. ## Dynamic override This is the recommended way to override the standard malloc interface. ### Dynamic Override on Linux, BSD On these ELF-based systems we preload the mimalloc shared library so all calls to the standard `malloc` interface are resolved to the _mimalloc_ library. ``` > env LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/libmimalloc.so myprogram ``` You can set extra environment variables to check that mimalloc is running, like: ``` > env MIMALLOC_VERBOSE=1 LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/libmimalloc.so myprogram ``` or run with the debug version to get detailed statistics: ``` > env MIMALLOC_SHOW_STATS=1 LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/libmimalloc-debug.so myprogram ``` ### Dynamic Override on MacOS On macOS we can also preload the mimalloc shared library so all calls to the standard `malloc` interface are resolved to the _mimalloc_ library. ``` > env DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES=/usr/lib/libmimalloc.dylib myprogram ``` Note that certain security restrictions may apply when doing this from the [shell](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/43941322/dyld-insert-libraries-ignored-when-calling-application-through-bash). ### Dynamic Override on Windows We use a separate redirection DLL to override mimalloc on Windows such that we redirect all malloc/free calls that go through the (dynamic) C runtime allocator, including those from other DLL's or libraries. As it intercepts all allocation calls on a low level, it can be used on large programs that include other 3rd party components. There are four requirements to make the overriding work well: 1. Use the C-runtime library as a DLL (using the `/MD` or `/MDd` switch). 2. Link your program explicitly with the `mimalloc.dll.lib` export library for the `mimalloc.dll`. (which must be compiled with `-DMI_OVERRIDE=ON`, which is the default though). To ensure the `mimalloc.dll` is actually loaded at run-time it is easiest to insert some call to the mimalloc API in the `main` function, like `mi_version()` (or use the `/include:mi_version` switch on the linker command, or similarly, `#pragma comment(linker, "/include:mi_version")` in some source file). See the `mimalloc-test-override` project for an example on how to use this. 3. The `mimalloc-redirect.dll` must be put in the same directory as the main `mimalloc.dll` at runtime (as it is a dependency of that DLL). The redirection DLL ensures that all calls to the C runtime malloc API get redirected to mimalloc functions (which reside in `mimalloc.dll`). 4. Ensure the `mimalloc.dll` comes as early as possible in the import list of the final executable (so it can intercept all potential allocations). You can use `minject -l ` to check this if needed. units.title: 单元三：核心数据结构——从堆层级到页与块

learning_goals: 跟踪 mi_malloc→_mi_theap_malloc_zero→mi_page_malloc_zero 的每一步
理解从 free list 头部弹出一个 block 只有几次内存访问
解释 forceinline/likely 等手段如何保证快路径的代码生成质量
lectures.practice_task: 在 alloc.c 中标注 mi_theap_malloc_small_zero 从进入函数到返回指针的全部语句，数出最少内存读写次数；用 -O2 编译生成汇编（MI_SEE_ASM=ON），对比快路径的指令条数。
lectures.title: mi_malloc 快路径：几条指令完成一次小对象分配
lectures.topic: 逐行精读 src/alloc.c 的 mi_theap_malloc_small_zero → mi_page_malloc_zero：pages_free_direct 查页、free list 弹出一个块、used 递增。

learning_goals: 描述 free list 耗尽后 mi_theap_malloc_generic 的完整补救流程
理解 mi_page_extend_free 延迟初始化块的意义（减少 memset 与缺页）
解释 generic_count/generic_collect_count 与 mi_option_generic_collect 的关系
lectures.practice_task: 在 debug 构建里连续分配同 size 块直到统计输出出现新的 page，结合 mi_page_fresh/mi_page_extend_free 源码解释：一个新页的块是「一次性全部初始化」还是「分批初始化」？写出证据。
lectures.title: 慢路径：mi_find_page、mi_page_fresh 与 free list 扩展
lectures.topic: 当快路径失败时：mi_theap_malloc_generic 如何在页队列里找候选页、扩展 free list（mi_page_extend_free）、申请新页（mi_page_fresh）并触发回收。

learning_goals: 说明大对象何时直接向 OS/arena 申请而非走 size class 页
理解 mi_arena_max_object_size 选项对 arena 使用的限制
分析大对象专用 mi_page_t 的 capacity/used 取值特殊性
lectures.practice_task: 写程序分别分配 512KB、2MB、64MB 的块，用 MIMALLOC_SHOW_STATS=1 观察 huge/arena 相关统计变化；再设 mi_option_arena_max_object_size 为 1MB 重跑，对比行为差异。
lectures.title: 大对象与巨大对象：mi_huge_page_alloc 与直接 OS 分配
lectures.topic: 超过 MI_LARGE_MAX_OBJ_SIZE 的对象走 mi_huge_page_alloc：每个对象一个专属页，内存直接来自 arena 或 OS，页结构如何退化使用。

learning_goals: 理解 realloc 原地扩展的条件（同页且剩余空间足够）
掌握自然对齐捷径与一般对齐回退路径的选择逻辑
会用 mi_malloc_aligned_at 实现带偏移的对齐分配
lectures.practice_task: 用 mi_posix_memalign 以 256 字节对齐分配 1KB，再用 mi_malloc_aligned_at 分配「距 4KB 边界偏移 64 字节」的块；打印地址验证对齐，并说明两条路径分别命中了 alloc-aligned.c 中的哪个分支。
lectures.title: realloc 家族与对齐分配：alloc-aligned.c 的取整策略
lectures.topic: 分析 mi_realloc 的原地扩展判断（mi_theap_realloc_zero_ex）与 mi_theap_realloc_zero_aligned 的对齐分配策略：自然对齐捷径、过度分配上限、_aligned_at 偏移版本，以及 posix_memalign 适配。

units.title: 单元四：分配主链路——mi_malloc 的快路径与慢路径

learning_goals: 读懂 mi_free_nonnull 中 xtid==0 等四个分支的判定条件
理解本线程 free 只做一次链表头插入而不碰原子操作
区分 mi_free_block_local 里 deferred 分支的进入条件
lectures.practice_task: 在 free.c 中给 mi_free_nonnull 的四个分支各写一行注释说明触发条件；再写一个单线程程序 free 一个块，用调试器单步确认走的是 mi_free_block_local 且无任何原子 CAS。
lectures.title: mi_free 快路径：本地 free 一次链表插入
lectures.topic: 精读 src/free.c 的 mi_free_nonnull：通过 page map 找页、比较 xthread_id 与当前线程 id 的异或结果分流到本地释放或跨线程释放。

learning_goals: 解释 CAS 推入 thread_free 单链表为何无需锁也不需 ABA 防护
理解所有权位让并发 free 顺手「认领」被遗弃页的巧妙设计
描述 thread_free 链表何时被拥有者线程收割回 free list
lectures.practice_task: 写一个双线程程序：线程 A 分配 100 万个小块，线程 B 全部 free；用 debug 统计对比它与「同线程分配同线程释放」版本的吞吐差异，并结合源码解释 free list 多碎片化为何让跨线程 free 依然便宜。
lectures.title: 跨线程 free：一次 CAS 推入 thread_free 链表
lectures.topic: 理解 mi_free_block_mt 如何用一个 CAS 把块挂到页的 xthread_free 链表、低位所有权位（MI_THREAD_FREE 语义）如何在 free 时原子认领页，以及拥有者线程在 page.c 中的收割时机。

learning_goals: 掌握 mi_register_deferred_free 回调的注册时机与触发节奏
理解 heartbeat 单调计数如何驱动运行时系统做有界回收
知道 deferred free 语义与普通 free 的差别（计数不减 used）
lectures.practice_task: 编写一个模拟引用计数运行时：注册 deferred free 回调打印调用序号，循环分配/释放 10 万个块，观察回调触发频率；再调整 mi_option_generic_collect 值对比触发节奏变化。
lectures.title: 延迟释放与心跳：为运行时系统提供的钩子
lectures.topic: 分析 mi_register_deferred_free 与 theap heartbeat 机制：local_free 链表如何实现单调心跳与延迟释放，供 Koka/Lean 等运行时在安全点批量回收。

units.title: 单元五：释放路径——本地 free、跨线程 free 与延迟回收

learning_goals: 列出 prim 接口的主要函数族（内存映射、commit、NUMA、TLS）
对照 unix 与 windows 实现说出 mmap 与 VirtualAlloc 的对应关系
理解独立抽象层如何支撑众多平台移植
lectures.practice_task: 对照 prim.h 接口，在 src/prim/unix/prim.c 与 src/prim/windows/prim.c 中各找出虚拟内存 reserve/commit 的实现函数，写一张「接口→两个平台实现」的对照表。
lectures.title: OS 原语抽象层：src/prim 如何隔离平台差异
lectures.topic: 讲解 include/mimalloc/prim.h 定义的操作系统原语接口与 src/prim/{unix,windows,osx,emscripten,wasi} 各实现，说明新平台移植只需实现这一层。

learning_goals: 区分 commit/decommit、purge(decommit)/reset(MADV_FREE/MADV_DONTNEED) 两对操作
理解 purge_delay 与 minimal_purge_size 对长时服务内存占用的调节作用
知道大页/巨页申请的适用场景与代价
lectures.practice_task: 写一个长循环分配释放程序，分别以 MIMALLOC_PURGE_DELAY=-1、1000、0 三种配置运行并记录峰值 RSS 与运行时间，结合 _mi_os_purge 源码解释三组数据的取舍。
lectures.title: os.c：commit/decommit/purge 与大页、NUMA
lectures.topic: 分析 src/os.c 的统一内存操作层：_mi_os_alloc/commit/purge 的语义、MIMALLOC_PURGE_DECOMMITS 的两种模式、_mi_os_alloc_huge_os_pages 与 NUMA 节点选择。

learning_goals: 说明 arena 默认 1GiB、slice 64KiB 的尺寸设计与 MI_MAX_ARENAS 上限
理解原子位图 find/set 区间操作如何实现无锁内存切分
会用 mi_manage_os_memory_ex 把自有内存纳入 mimalloc 管理
lectures.practice_task: 调用 mi_arenas_print()（或 mi_debug_show_arenas）观察分配前后的 arena 状态；再用 mi_reserve_os_memory_ex 预留 64MiB 独占 arena，并用 mi_heap_new_in_arena 建堆验证分配确实落在该 arena（mi_arena_contains）。
lectures.title: arena：1GiB 内存区、64KiB slice 与原子位图分配
lectures.topic: 精读 src/arena.c：arena 的保留与扩张、slice 按位图分配、eager commit 策略，以及 bitmap.h 中原子位图的区间查找与置位算法。

learning_goals: 解释线程退出时其页面为何被 abandon 而非立刻回收
描述 arena 中 abandoned 位图如何让其他线程快速认领整页
理解 retire_expire 与 purge 到期如何降低内存驻留
lectures.practice_task: 构建 test/test-stress 或自写的多线程反复创建销毁线程的压测，用 MIMALLOC_SHOW_STATS=1 观察 abandoned/reclaim 计数；再设 MIMALLOC_PAGE_RECLAIM_ON_FREE 的不同值对比 reclaimed 页数变化并解释。
lectures.title: abandon 与 reclaim：线程间共享内存的终极手段
lectures.topic: 理解 v3 的页面遗弃/认领机制：线程结束时 theap 的页面进入 abandoned 状态、arena 级 pages_abandoned 位图索引、其他线程按 size class 认领（mi_arena_try_claim_abandoned、free 时触发 reclaim）。

units.title: 单元六：内存管理层——prim 抽象、OS 页与 arena

learning_goals: 解释首次分配如何触发 mi_process_init 的 do-once 初始化
理解 main heap、tld、theap 之间的创建顺序
知道进程退出时 mi_process_done 的清理与统计输出时机
lectures.practice_task: 用 MIMALLOC_VERBOSE=1 运行最小 mi_malloc 程序，对照 init.c 里的 mi_process_init_once 打印顺序，在纸上排出「选项解析→os 初始化→arena 保留→主堆建立→TLS 绑定」的时间线。
lectures.title: 初始化流程：从第一次 mi_malloc 到 mi_process_done
lectures.topic: 分析 src/init.c：constructor 与 do-once 模式、mi_process_init 的步骤（选项、OS、arena、主堆）、mi_thread_init/mi_thread_done 的线程生命周期、退出时 mi_process_done 的统计与回收。

learning_goals: 说出各平台 TLS 策略的差异与选择依据
解释默认 theap 指针的获取代价为何决定了分配快路径下限
理解线程结束时 TLS destructor 如何联动 _mi_thread_done
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 prim-tls.c 中 MI_TLS_* 分支的宏条件，画出 Linux(pthread) 与 Windows(TLS slot) 两条路径获取默认 theap 的调用图；再统计在你的平台上 _mi_theap_default_get 展开后约需几次内存访问。
lectures.title: 线程本地存储：默认 theap 的查找与缓存
lectures.topic: 讲解线程如何拿到自己的 mi_theap_t：include/mimalloc/prim-tls.h 与 src/prim/prim-tls.c 中多种 TLS 实现策略（局部动态、pthread、Windows slot），以及 _mi_theap_default_set/_mi_theap_cached_set 的两级缓存。

learning_goals: 掌握 heap 与 theap 的创建/销毁 API 及引用计数语义
理解 v3 跨线程堆分配相对 v2 的改进点
会用 mi_heap_set_default 切换默认堆并用 mi_heap_destroy 一次性释放
lectures.practice_task: 参照 test/test-stress-heaps.c 编写：主线程建 3 个堆并分别设为默认堆后交由 3 个工作线程分配对象，最后 mi_heap_destroy 整体释放；用统计验证销毁后堆内存归零。
lectures.title: 一等堆：mi_heap_new/delete/destroy 与跨线程分配
lectures.topic: 分析 v3 的一等堆实现：src/heap.c 的堆生命周期、src/theap.c 中 _mi_theap_create/_mi_theap_alloc 如何让任意线程在同一个堆上分配、堆销毁时整堆一次性释放。

learning_goals: 解释 subproc 如何隔离 arena 与统计信息
掌握 mi_subproc_add_current_thread 的调用时机约束
理解子进程销毁时其堆与内存的回收边界
lectures.practice_task: 参照 test/test-stress-subprocs.c 写一个最小示例：创建 subproc、把工作线程加入、在其堆里分配后 mi_subproc_delete 销毁，用统计对比主 subproc 的内存是否不受影响。
lectures.title: 子进程（subproc）：为 CPython 多解释器设计的隔离
lectures.topic: 了解 mi_subproc_t：一个进程内多个互相隔离的分配域，各自持有 arena 集合与主堆，CPython 用它实现多解释器内存隔离。

units.title: 单元七：初始化、线程与 v3 一等堆

learning_goals: 理解 mi_atomic_* 宏如何映射到 C11 原子与 MSVC 内建
掌握 mi_lock_t 无锁自旋锁的获取/退避/释放流程
区分 relaxed/acquire/release 三种序在 page map 与 thread_free 上的用法
lectures.practice_task: 统计仓库中 mi_atomic_cas_strong/weak、acquire/release 的典型使用位置各 3 处，说明每处为何选择该内存序；再用 MI_DEBUG_TSAN 构建跑一次 test-stress 验证无数据竞争告警。
lectures.title: 原子抽象与 mi_lock：无锁基础设施
lectures.topic: 阅读 include/mimalloc/atomic.h：跨编译器的原子操作封装、内存序选择，以及基于 CAS 的 mi_lock_t 自旋锁（含指数退避）在 arena/heap 中的使用。

learning_goals: 论证「每页多条 free list」如何把竞争分散到整个堆
量化对比单一大 free list 与分片方案在最坏情形的差异
把设计要点映射到 mimalloc 在 xmalloc-testN/sh8bench 上的优势
lectures.practice_task: 实现一个玩具分配器（每 size class 一条全局 free list vs 每页一条），用双线程分别只分配/只释放各 100 万块，测量两种实现的吞吐比，并写一段分析说明分片为何胜出。
lectures.title: free list 分片与多分片：mimalloc 的核心创新
lectures.topic: 从设计层面综合已学代码，解读 readme 中的两大 idea：free list sharding（每页独立 free list 提升局部性）与 multi-sharding（每页再分 local/thread 两条 list 消除跨线程竞争），并联系技术报告中的 benchmark 结论。

learning_goals: 读懂 mi_bitmap_find/try_set_from 区间位图算法
理解 binned bitmap（bbitmap）分桶查找如何避免大位图线性扫描
解释 v3.5 用更快原子操作优化 arena 位图的动机
lectures.practice_task: 构造一个 1024 位的 mi_bitmap_t（参照 arena.c 用法），手动执行「找 8 个连续空闲位并占用」操作若干次，打印每步位图状态，验证边界（尾部不足 8 位）时返回 false。
lectures.title: 原子位图内部：bitmap.c 的区间查找与 x64 优化
lectures.topic: 深入 src/bitmap.c：逐字位图操作、原子 test-and-set、查找连续空闲区间的算法，以及 BMI1/2（tzcnt/blsi）等指令优化。

units.title: 单元八：并发与底层原语——原子、分片设计与位图

learning_goals: 理解 MI_SECURE 下 free list 指针与随机 key 异或编码的原理
说明 guard page 如何阻断越界读写对元数据的攻击
分析 double-free 检测路径的代价与收益
lectures.practice_task: 构建 MI_SECURE=ON 版本，写程序故意 double free 与越界写；对比 release 版本的行为差异，并从源码指出是哪段检查发现了问题。
lectures.title: 安全模式：加密 free list、guard page 与双重释放检测
lectures.topic: 分析 MI_SECURE 构建下的防护：free list 指针加密（页级随机 key）、元数据 guard page（os.c 中 _mi_os_secure_guard_page_*）、随机化初始化与 double-free 检测。

learning_goals: 理解 mi_padding_t 结构与 byte 级越界检测原理
掌握 guarded 采样的调参组合（rate/seed/min/max/precise）
知道 debug 构建里各种断言（mi_assert_internal）的检查范围
lectures.practice_task: 用 debug 构建（默认含 padding 检查）写一个越界 1 字节的用例运行 test-wrong 风格验证；再开 MI_GUARDED=ON 配 MIMALLOC_GUARDED_SAMPLE_RATE=1 复现同一越界被 guard page 当场捕获。
lectures.title: debug 模式、padding 校验与 guarded 采样
lectures.topic: 讲解 Debug 构建的运行时检查（padding 校验 mi_verify_padding、损坏链表检测、无效指针检测）与 MI_GUARDED 按采样率在对象后放置 OS guard page 的机制。

learning_goals: 读懂 MIMALLOC_SHOW_STATS 输出的 bin/page/arena/process 四段报表
掌握按 heap/theap/subproc 粒度取数的 API 差异
能用 JSON 输出做自动化内存回归监控
lectures.practice_task: 为一个多线程程序在退出前调用 mi_stats_get 取进程级统计，再用 mi_heap_stats_get 取各堆统计并求和对比，解释两者为何存在差异（元数据归属）；再导出一份 JSON 留档。
lectures.title: 统计系统：从 mi_stats_t 到 JSON 导出
lectures.topic: 分析 src/stats.c：mi_stat_count_t 的 peak/total/current 语义、theap→heap→subproc 的统计合并、mi_stats_print_out 与实验性 mi_stat_get/mi_stat_get_json 接口。

learning_goals: 掌握 mi_heap_visit_blocks 遍历所有存活块的用法与约束
理解 abandoned 页为何默认不被遍历
说明 v3 相对旧版 heap-walking 的效率改进来源
lectures.practice_task: 用 mi_heap_visit_blocks 实现一个简易「堆快照」工具：分配一批对象后打印每个 size class 的存活块数；再故意制造内存泄漏（分配不释放），验证快照能定位到泄漏的 size class。
lectures.title: 堆遍历：visit_blocks 与 GC 集成
lectures.topic: 分析 src/theap.c 的 _mi_theap_area_visit_blocks / mi_theap_visit_blocks：如何沿页队列和 free list 推断每个块的存活状态，CPython 的 GC 如何借它做根集扫描。

learning_goals: 掌握 MI_TRACK_VALGRIND/ASAN/ETW 三种插桩构建的用途
理解 mimalloc 在各类基准上的强弱项及其设计根源
能独立复现一次 LD_PRELOAD 对比测试
lectures.practice_task: 分别构建 ASAN 版（MI_TRACK_ASAN=ON）与普通版运行 test-wrong；再用 release 构建对一个真实程序做「系统 malloc vs LD_PRELOAD=mimalloc」的耗时对比，写一份简短评测报告。
lectures.title: 工具链与基准：valgrind/ASAN/ETW 与性能评估
lectures.topic: 汇总工具生态：MI_TRACK_VALGRIND/ASAN/ETW 构建配合外部工具做泄漏与越界检测，readme 的基准方法论（cfrac/leanN/xmalloc-testN 等场景含义），以及 vcpkg/find_package 集成发布方式。

units.title: 单元九：安全、观测与工程实践

data.head: cd69707c3ca01a4c5fb358e8b92a710554f15356
data.rationale: mimalloc v3 是一个约万行级 C 语言通用内存分配器，核心难度集中在「heap→theap→page→block 的四层数据模型、free list 双碎片化（local_free/thread_free）的无锁并发设计、arena+原子位图的内存管理」三处。因此学习路线先让读者从零跑起来并会用 mi_ API 与 malloc 覆盖（u1-u2 入门层），再自顶向下拆解核心数据结构（u3），然后沿 mi_malloc/mi_free 两条真实调用链逐文件精读（u4-u5），接着深入 OS 原语抽象、arena 与 abandon/reclaim 内存管理（u6），理解初始化、TLS 与 v3 新增的一等 heap/subproc 机制（u7），最后进入专家层：原子原语、碎片化设计原理、位图实现（u8），以及安全模式、统计观测、调试工具与基准评估（u9）。每一讲只解决一个问题、绑定 1-6 个真实源码文件并配一个动手任务，依赖关系严格按「先用起来→看结构→读链路→抠并发→做工程」递进。

learning_goals: 说出 mimalloc 的定位、主要特性与典型应用场景
区分 v1/v2/v3 三个维护分支的差异
理解 free list sharding、eager page purging 等核心设计关键词
lectures.practice_task: 通读 readme.md 的特性清单与 Releases 小节，写一段 200 字总结：mimalloc 相比 glibc ptmalloc 解决了哪些问题；并列出 v3 相对 v2 的三个主要改进点。
lectures.title: mimalloc 是什么：一个高性能通用分配器的定位与设计
lectures.topic: 介绍 mimalloc 的定位、设计亮点（free list sharding、多级碎片化、eager purging、一等堆）以及 v1/v2/v3 三个版本的差异。

learning_goals: 用 cmake 完成 release/debug/secure 三种构建
理解 MI_OVERRIDE、MI_SECURE、MI_GUARDED 等构建开关的作用
知道 src/static.c 单文件编译方式与产物形态（.so/.a/.o）
lectures.practice_task: 在本地克隆仓库并执行 mkdir -p out/release && cd out/release && cmake ../.. && make 完成 release 构建；再用 -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug 构建 debug 版本，记录两种版本生成的库文件名差异。
lectures.title: 构建与运行：cmake、debug/secure 模式与单文件编译
lectures.topic: 讲解如何用 cmake 构建 mimalloc（release/debug/secure/guarded），构建产物有哪些，以及 src/static.c 如何把整个库合并成单目标文件。

learning_goals: 画出 src/、include/mimalloc/、src/prim/、test/ 的职责划分图
说明 alloc.c、free.c、page.c、arena.c 各自承担的角色
理解 src/prim OS 抽象层为何按 unix/windows/osx 等子目录组织
lectures.practice_task: 浏览 src/ 下每个 .c 文件顶部的版权注释与主要函数名，手工绘制一张模块依赖草图，标出你认为的「分配主链路」会经过哪几个文件，并在后续单元中验证。
lectures.title: 目录结构与代码地图：src、include、prim、test 的分工
lectures.topic: 梳理项目目录结构，建立每个源文件到其职责的映射，帮助读者在后续阅读时快速定位。

learning_goals: 正确包含 mimalloc.h 并链接 libmimalloc
使用 mi_malloc/mi_zalloc/mi_calloc/mi_strdup/mi_free 完成一次完整分配周期
用 MIMALLOC_SHOW_STATS=1 观察并解读分配统计输出
lectures.practice_task: 参照 test/test-api.c 编写一个小程序：分别用 mi_malloc、mi_zalloc、mi_calloc、mi_strdup 分配不同大小的内存块再释放，用 MIMALLOC_SHOW_STATS=1 运行并解释输出中每个 bin 行的含义。
lectures.title: 第一次使用 mi_ API：从 mi_malloc 到 MIMALLOC_SHOW_STATS
lectures.topic: 通过 include/mimalloc.h 公共 API 与 test/test-api.c 示例，学会直接使用 mi_ 前缀的分配接口并观察统计输出。

units.title: 单元一：走进 mimalloc——定位、构建与第一个程序

learning_goals: 理解 src/alloc-override.c 中如何定义与 malloc 同名的导出符号
掌握 Linux LD_PRELOAD 与 macOS DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES 两种覆盖方式
理解 mimalloc-override.h 宏替换方案的风险（跨堆指针混用）
lectures.practice_task: 构建后用 env MIMALLOC_VERBOSE=1 LD_PRELOAD=<libmimalloc.so 路径> ./myprogram 运行任意一个已有 C 程序（如 test 里的 main-override），确认输出中出现 mimalloc 的版本信息，证明覆盖成功。
lectures.title: 动态覆盖 malloc：LD_PRELOAD 与 alloc-override.c
lectures.topic: 讲解 mimalloc 如何在不修改代码的前提下替换系统 malloc/free，包括 ELF 预加载、静态目标文件优先链接与 mimalloc-override.h 宏重定义三种途径。

learning_goals: 会用 mimalloc-new-delete.h 全局替换 new/delete
理解 mi_stl_allocator 与 mi_heap_stl_allocator 的区别及适用场景
知道为何 new/delete 覆盖头只能包含进一个源文件
lectures.practice_task: 写一个 C++ 程序，在唯一的 main.cpp 中 include <mimalloc-new-delete.h>，用 std::vector<int, mi_stl_allocator<int>> 存放 100 万个元素；再用 MIMALLOC_SHOW_STATS=1 验证分配确实走了 mimalloc。
lectures.title: C++ 集成：new/delete 覆盖与 mi_stl_allocator
lectures.topic: 学习在 C++ 项目中集成 mimalloc 的两种方式：覆盖全局 new/delete（mimalloc-new-delete.h）以及使用实现 std::allocator 接口的 mi_stl_allocator / mi_heap_stl_allocator。

learning_goals: 理解 mi_option_t 枚举中稳定选项与高级选项的划分
掌握 MIMALLOC_ 前缀环境变量到选项的映射规则
会用 mi_option_set/mi_option_get 在程序内调参
lectures.practice_task: 在程序中调用 mi_option_set(mi_option_purge_delay, 0) 与 mi_option_enable(mi_option_verbose)，再分别用环境变量 MIMALLOC_PURGE_DELAY=0 和 MIMALLOC_VERBOSE=1 复现同样效果，对比两种方式的输出。
lectures.title: 选项系统：环境变量、mi_option 与运行时调参
lectures.topic: 解析 src/options.c 的选项解析机制：环境变量 MIMALLOC_*、mi_option_get/set 编程接口，以及 purge_delay、arena_eager_commit 等关键调优项。

units.title: 单元二：把 mimalloc 用起来——覆盖标准 malloc 与配置调优

learning_goals: 准确描述 subproc/heap/theap/page/block 五层的所有权关系
解释 v3 为何引入 theap（线程本地堆）这一层
理解 mi_memid_t 如何记录每块内存的来源（arena/OS）
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 types.h 中五个结构体的字段注释，画一张层次 ownership 图；并回答：一个普通线程第一次 mi_malloc 时，从 heap_main 到最终 block 会经过哪些结构？
lectures.title: 堆的层级模型：subproc → heap → theap → page queue → block
lectures.topic: 建立 v3 核心对象模型的心智地图：mi_subproc_t（子进程）、mi_heap_t（一等堆）、mi_theap_t（线程本地堆）、mi_page_queue_t（size class 队列）、mi_page_t（页）与 mi_block_t（块）。

learning_goals: 说出 free/local_free/thread_free 三个链表的分工与迁移时机
推导 used、capacity、reserved 与实际存活块数的关系式
理解 xthread_id 低位存放 page flags 的位技巧
lectures.practice_task: 根据 types.h 注释推导：当 used - thread_free 数 == capacity 时页面处于什么状态？写一个小测试分配 1000 个同 size 块再全部释放，用 debug 构建的统计输出验证你的推断。
lectures.title: mi_page_t 深入：一个页的三条 free list
lectures.topic: 精读 mi_page_s 结构：free/local_free/thread_free 三条链表的含义、used/capacity/reserved 的不变式、xthread_id 与 xthread_free 中标志位的编码。

learning_goals: 理解 _mi_bin 如何把请求尺寸映射到 size class
说明 pages_free_direct 数组如何让小对象分配 O(1) 定位到页
区分 small/medium/large/huge 对象的尺寸边界（如 MI_SMALL_MAX_OBJ_SIZE）
lectures.practice_task: 在 debug 构建下运行一个分配 1B~1MB 各种尺寸的程序并打开统计，对照 MI_SMALL_MAX_OBJ_SIZE 等宏，写出一个尺寸→分类（small/medium/large/huge）的判断表格并用输出验证。
lectures.title: size class 与 bin：page-queue 的组织方式
lectures.topic: 理解 mi_bin 大小分类、MI_BIN_COUNT 个页队列的组织，以及 mi_theap_s.pages_free_direct 直接索引数组如何加速小对象分配。

learning_goals: 说明 free 操作如何借助 page map 从指针反查 mi_page_t
理解 64KiB arena slice 粒度对 page map 体积的影响
知道 MI_PAGE_META_IS_ALIGNED 模式下如何免查 page map
lectures.practice_task: 根据 internal.h 中 2-level page map 的注释计算：48 位地址空间下顶层需要多少字节？再阅读 page-map.c 的 mi_page_map_ensure_committed，解释按需 commit 如何避免一次性付出全部内存。
lectures.title: page map：从任意指针找回它的页
lectures.topic: 分析 src/page-map.c 与 internal.h 中两级基数树的实现：指针→mi_page_t 的 O(1) 映射、按需 commit，以及 MI_PAGE_META_IS_ALIGNED 时直接对齐定位元数据的快速路径。

units.title: 单元三：核心数据结构——从堆层级到页与块

learning_goals: 跟踪 mi_malloc→_mi_theap_malloc_zero→mi_page_malloc_zero 的每一步
理解从 free list 头部弹出一个 block 只有几次内存访问
解释 forceinline/likely 等手段如何保证快路径的代码生成质量
lectures.practice_task: 在 alloc.c 中标注 mi_theap_malloc_small_zero 从进入函数到返回指针的全部语句，数出最少内存读写次数；用 -O2 编译生成汇编（MI_SEE_ASM=ON），对比快路径的指令条数。
lectures.title: mi_malloc 快路径：几条指令完成一次小对象分配
lectures.topic: 逐行精读 src/alloc.c 的 mi_theap_malloc_small_zero → mi_page_malloc_zero：pages_free_direct 查页、free list 弹出一个块、used 递增。

learning_goals: 描述 free list 耗尽后 mi_theap_malloc_generic 的完整补救流程
理解 mi_page_extend_free 延迟初始化块的意义（减少 memset 与缺页）
解释 generic_count/generic_collect_count 与 mi_option_generic_collect 的关系
lectures.practice_task: 在 debug 构建里连续分配同 size 块直到统计输出出现新的 page，结合 mi_page_fresh/mi_page_extend_free 源码解释：一个新页的块是「一次性全部初始化」还是「分批初始化」？写出证据。
lectures.title: 慢路径：mi_find_page、mi_page_fresh 与 free list 扩展
lectures.topic: 当快路径失败时：mi_theap_malloc_generic 如何在页队列里找候选页、扩展 free list（mi_page_extend_free）、申请新页（mi_page_fresh）并触发回收。

learning_goals: 说明大对象何时直接向 OS/arena 申请而非走 size class 页
理解 mi_arena_max_object_size 选项对 arena 使用的限制
分析大对象专用 mi_page_t 的 capacity/used 取值特殊性
lectures.practice_task: 写程序分别分配 512KB、2MB、64MB 的块，用 MIMALLOC_SHOW_STATS=1 观察 huge/arena 相关统计变化；再设 mi_option_arena_max_object_size 为 1MB 重跑，对比行为差异。
lectures.title: 大对象与巨大对象：mi_huge_page_alloc 与直接 OS 分配
lectures.topic: 超过 MI_LARGE_MAX_OBJ_SIZE 的对象走 mi_huge_page_alloc：每个对象一个专属页，内存直接来自 arena 或 OS，页结构如何退化使用。

learning_goals: 理解 realloc 原地扩展的条件（同页且剩余空间足够）
掌握自然对齐捷径与一般对齐回退路径的选择逻辑
会用 mi_malloc_aligned_at 实现带偏移的对齐分配
lectures.practice_task: 用 mi_posix_memalign 以 256 字节对齐分配 1KB，再用 mi_malloc_aligned_at 分配「距 4KB 边界偏移 64 字节」的块；打印地址验证对齐，并说明两条路径分别命中了 alloc-aligned.c 中的哪个分支。
lectures.title: realloc 家族与对齐分配：alloc-aligned.c 的取整策略
lectures.topic: 分析 mi_realloc 的原地扩展判断（mi_theap_realloc_zero_ex）与 mi_theap_realloc_zero_aligned 的对齐分配策略：自然对齐捷径、过度分配上限、_aligned_at 偏移版本，以及 posix_memalign 适配。

units.title: 单元四：分配主链路——mi_malloc 的快路径与慢路径

learning_goals: 读懂 mi_free_nonnull 中 xtid==0 等四个分支的判定条件
理解本线程 free 只做一次链表头插入而不碰原子操作
区分 mi_free_block_local 里 deferred 分支的进入条件
lectures.practice_task: 在 free.c 中给 mi_free_nonnull 的四个分支各写一行注释说明触发条件；再写一个单线程程序 free 一个块，用调试器单步确认走的是 mi_free_block_local 且无任何原子 CAS。
lectures.title: mi_free 快路径：本地 free 一次链表插入
lectures.topic: 精读 src/free.c 的 mi_free_nonnull：通过 page map 找页、比较 xthread_id 与当前线程 id 的异或结果分流到本地释放或跨线程释放。

learning_goals: 解释 CAS 推入 thread_free 单链表为何无需锁也不需 ABA 防护
理解所有权位让并发 free 顺手「认领」被遗弃页的巧妙设计
描述 thread_free 链表何时被拥有者线程收割回 free list
lectures.practice_task: 写一个双线程程序：线程 A 分配 100 万个小块，线程 B 全部 free；用 debug 统计对比它与「同线程分配同线程释放」版本的吞吐差异，并结合源码解释 free list 多碎片化为何让跨线程 free 依然便宜。
lectures.title: 跨线程 free：一次 CAS 推入 thread_free 链表
lectures.topic: 理解 mi_free_block_mt 如何用一个 CAS 把块挂到页的 xthread_free 链表、低位所有权位（MI_THREAD_FREE 语义）如何在 free 时原子认领页，以及拥有者线程在 page.c 中的收割时机。

learning_goals: 掌握 mi_register_deferred_free 回调的注册时机与触发节奏
理解 heartbeat 单调计数如何驱动运行时系统做有界回收
知道 deferred free 语义与普通 free 的差别（计数不减 used）
lectures.practice_task: 编写一个模拟引用计数运行时：注册 deferred free 回调打印调用序号，循环分配/释放 10 万个块，观察回调触发频率；再调整 mi_option_generic_collect 值对比触发节奏变化。
lectures.title: 延迟释放与心跳：为运行时系统提供的钩子
lectures.topic: 分析 mi_register_deferred_free 与 theap heartbeat 机制：local_free 链表如何实现单调心跳与延迟释放，供 Koka/Lean 等运行时在安全点批量回收。

units.title: 单元五：释放路径——本地 free、跨线程 free 与延迟回收

learning_goals: 列出 prim 接口的主要函数族（内存映射、commit、NUMA、TLS）
对照 unix 与 windows 实现说出 mmap 与 VirtualAlloc 的对应关系
理解独立抽象层如何支撑众多平台移植
lectures.practice_task: 对照 prim.h 接口，在 src/prim/unix/prim.c 与 src/prim/windows/prim.c 中各找出虚拟内存 reserve/commit 的实现函数，写一张「接口→两个平台实现」的对照表。
lectures.title: OS 原语抽象层：src/prim 如何隔离平台差异
lectures.topic: 讲解 include/mimalloc/prim.h 定义的操作系统原语接口与 src/prim/{unix,windows,osx,emscripten,wasi} 各实现，说明新平台移植只需实现这一层。

learning_goals: 区分 commit/decommit、purge(decommit)/reset(MADV_FREE/MADV_DONTNEED) 两对操作
理解 purge_delay 与 minimal_purge_size 对长时服务内存占用的调节作用
知道大页/巨页申请的适用场景与代价
lectures.practice_task: 写一个长循环分配释放程序，分别以 MIMALLOC_PURGE_DELAY=-1、1000、0 三种配置运行并记录峰值 RSS 与运行时间，结合 _mi_os_purge 源码解释三组数据的取舍。
lectures.title: os.c：commit/decommit/purge 与大页、NUMA
lectures.topic: 分析 src/os.c 的统一内存操作层：_mi_os_alloc/commit/purge 的语义、MIMALLOC_PURGE_DECOMMITS 的两种模式、_mi_os_alloc_huge_os_pages 与 NUMA 节点选择。

learning_goals: 说明 arena 默认 1GiB、slice 64KiB 的尺寸设计与 MI_MAX_ARENAS 上限
理解原子位图 find/set 区间操作如何实现无锁内存切分
会用 mi_manage_os_memory_ex 把自有内存纳入 mimalloc 管理
lectures.practice_task: 调用 mi_arenas_print()（或 mi_debug_show_arenas）观察分配前后的 arena 状态；再用 mi_reserve_os_memory_ex 预留 64MiB 独占 arena，并用 mi_heap_new_in_arena 建堆验证分配确实落在该 arena（mi_arena_contains）。
lectures.title: arena：1GiB 内存区、64KiB slice 与原子位图分配
lectures.topic: 精读 src/arena.c：arena 的保留与扩张、slice 按位图分配、eager commit 策略，以及 bitmap.h 中原子位图的区间查找与置位算法。

learning_goals: 解释线程退出时其页面为何被 abandon 而非立刻回收
描述 arena 中 abandoned 位图如何让其他线程快速认领整页
理解 retire_expire 与 purge 到期如何降低内存驻留
lectures.practice_task: 构建 test/test-stress 或自写的多线程反复创建销毁线程的压测，用 MIMALLOC_SHOW_STATS=1 观察 abandoned/reclaim 计数；再设 MIMALLOC_PAGE_RECLAIM_ON_FREE 的不同值对比 reclaimed 页数变化并解释。
lectures.title: abandon 与 reclaim：线程间共享内存的终极手段
lectures.topic: 理解 v3 的页面遗弃/认领机制：线程结束时 theap 的页面进入 abandoned 状态、arena 级 pages_abandoned 位图索引、其他线程按 size class 认领（mi_arena_try_claim_abandoned、free 时触发 reclaim）。

units.title: 单元六：内存管理层——prim 抽象、OS 页与 arena

learning_goals: 解释首次分配如何触发 mi_process_init 的 do-once 初始化
理解 main heap、tld、theap 之间的创建顺序
知道进程退出时 mi_process_done 的清理与统计输出时机
lectures.practice_task: 用 MIMALLOC_VERBOSE=1 运行最小 mi_malloc 程序，对照 init.c 里的 mi_process_init_once 打印顺序，在纸上排出「选项解析→os 初始化→arena 保留→主堆建立→TLS 绑定」的时间线。
lectures.title: 初始化流程：从第一次 mi_malloc 到 mi_process_done
lectures.topic: 分析 src/init.c：constructor 与 do-once 模式、mi_process_init 的步骤（选项、OS、arena、主堆）、mi_thread_init/mi_thread_done 的线程生命周期、退出时 mi_process_done 的统计与回收。

learning_goals: 说出各平台 TLS 策略的差异与选择依据
解释默认 theap 指针的获取代价为何决定了分配快路径下限
理解线程结束时 TLS destructor 如何联动 _mi_thread_done
